description: Jesteśmy drużyną CTRL z Koła Naukowego Machine Learning Politechniki Rzeszowskiej! Łączymy pasję do AI, analizy danych i inżynierii z eksploracją kosmosu. W wyzwaniu Lunar Landing Site Navigator tworzymy intuicyjną aplikację webową symulującą potencjał ładowania solarnego lądowników na Księżycu. Mamy już gotowy plan i model danych!Szukamy wsparcia w: Frontend (JS/React), UI/UX Design oraz Pitch/Video. Dołącz do nas i stwórzmy razem kosmiczny projekt!
summary: Marswalk Planner is a layered map and route planner for a crewed walk (EVA) on Mars, built for the boxwork ridges of lower Mount Sharp in Gale crater. For one 2 x 2 km patch we stack NASA data: the HiRISE 1 m terrain model and 25 cm image, CRISM spectra for water-bearing minerals (MRO), THEMIS night-time infrared for loose sand, and the radiation dose measured by RAD on Curiosity, turned into a dose map from how much sky the terrain hides. These layers become a cost map for a person in a suit; ground that is too steep or rough is closed. A* finds the cheapest route, and a mission planner orders the science targets, keeps an oxygen reserve and hands steep targets to a rover's robotic arm. It all runs live in ROS 2, with a habitat dashboard, a HUD prototype for XREAL glasses and an Isaac Sim simulation of the astronaut and support rover. Today's Mars maps show regions, but an EVA is a few kilometres where one cliff matters. Our map answers the crew's question: which way can a person walk safely, and what will it cost in time, oxygen and dose?
details:
Marswalk Planner turns NASA data for one 2 x 2 km patch of lower Mount Sharp (Gale crater) into a plan for a crewed walk on Mars. From HiRISE we compute slope, roughness and open sky. CRISM shows water bound in minerals, THEMIS night-time infrared shows likely loose sand, and Curiosity's RAD dose rate is turned into a dose map from the sky view. These layers form a cost map for a person in a spacesuit, where ground steeper than 25 degrees or rougher than 2 m is closed. A* finds the cheapest route. A mission planner orders the science targets.

How it works: a Python pipeline builds the layers. ROS 2 Humble nodes publish the cost maps and the route. An aiohttp WebSocket server streams live state to a web dashboard built with Three.js, with a 3D map, layers and a mission tab. Isaac Sim 5.1 simulates NASA's Z2 spacesuit walking the planned route, with a support rover carrying a robotic arm that samples where the planner closes the ground. A head-up display prototype is written for XREAL One glasses.

Impact: current Mars maps show whole regions, but a crew needs direction, time, oxygen and dose for a route a few kilometres long. The same pipeline can use lunar LRO data and suits Earth analog missions.

Tools: Python, JavaScript, HTML and CSS; Docker for ROS 2; NVIDIA Isaac Sim; Autodesk Inventor for the rover CAD models. Hardware: a laptop with an NVIDIA RTX 3050 (6 GB).

Limits we state openly: cost weights and limits are our assumptions; dose is a model, not a measurement at each place; THEMIS and CRISM are coarse, so they show trends, not single dunes or rocks; the HUD is a prototype.
